# Vertical overlay: Wholesale Trade

**Level:** NAICS 2022 sector 42 (parent vertical)
**Primary industry for Cris Santos Company:** NAICS 423430 Computer and Computer Peripheral Equipment and Software Merchant Wholesalers. IT hardware and software wholesale distributor serving commercial and federal (DoD) customers.
**Primary system:** Order management, warehouse, and reseller portal (ERP)

## Regulators and sector risk management agency
Federal Trade Commission (general data security/privacy enforcement); Department of Defense (CMMC/DFARS for defense-supply-chain distributors); U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CTPAT supply chain security, voluntary); Securities and Exchange Commission (public wholesalers); State attorneys general / California Privacy Protection Agency

## Primary regulation for the gap analysis (P03)
**NIST SP 800-171 R2 via CMMC Level 2 / DFARS 252.204-7012**, 32 CFR 170.14; 48 CFR 252.204-7012. For supply-chain-focused wholesalers, the most prescriptive, auditable and contractually enforced US control set is NIST SP 800-171 R2 (110 requirements) as required by DFARS 7012 and assessed under CMMC Level 2 (Phase 1 live since Nov 10, 2025). It flows down to subcontractors and distributors handling CUI. Wholesalers with no federal/defense business should instead use CISA CPGs 2.0 / NIST CSF 2.0 plus CTPAT MSC cybersecurity criteria as the benchmark, because no sector-wide federal cyber rule applies to wholesale trade.
Source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-32/part-170

## Sector context
- **Sensitive data:** Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and Federal Contract Information (FCI); Covered defense information / export-controlled technical data; Customer and supplier commercial data, pricing, EDI transaction data; B2B payment card and bank account data; Employee PII; Import/export filings and trade data
- **Critical systems:** ERP (order-to-cash, procure-to-pay); Warehouse management systems (WMS); EDI/VAN and supplier/customer portals; Transportation management systems (TMS); Distribution-center OT (conveyors, sortation, automated storage); Customs filing integrations (ACE)
- **Sector AI rules and guidance:** None identified beyond cross-sector obligations
- **Assurance alternatives to SOC 2:** None noted
- **Scenario incident (P08):** Supplier compromise introducing tampered or counterfeit products into distribution
- **Scenario AI use case (P10):** Demand forecasting and automated reordering

## Notes
No sector-specific federal cybersecurity regulator for wholesale trade; obligations are driven by customer contracts (DoD/federal), cross-sector laws (FTC Act, state privacy/breach laws, SEC for public companies), and voluntary CTPAT. DOJ 28 CFR 202 (bulk sensitive data) may apply if data/vendor arrangements involve countries of concern (see n51). Pharmaceutical wholesale distributors also face DSCSA traceability obligations (not researched here). Verified 2026-09-25.
